name: Yuppie demographic designation
description: Rapid circulation and repudiation of an aspirational urban-professional demographic label in 1980s consumer and political discourse.
cause_of_death: Materialism and gentrification associations turned the label pejorative; the 1987 crash preceded a reported 1991 public death declaration.

sources.title: Yuppie: Definition, History, Characteristics, and Gentrification
sources.note: Emily Kendall article inspected. Gives possible 1980 print appearance, Newsweek 1984 prominence, negative connotations, and TIME 1991 death declaration. Dates are event anchors, not frequencies.

entries.gloss: A fashionable label for an ambitious urban professional associated with material consumption.

examples.text: Let us give the yuppies a presentation they will remember.

entries.rationale: Britannica records possible print appearance in 1980, the 1984 year-of-the-yuppie declaration, and the 1991 death declaration following negative associations and the 1987 crash. Peak 1984 is an editorial prominence anchor; fade 1992 is estimated and does not imply the word vanished. Expansion variants belong to this entry rather than inflating the corpus. Context hints require an explicit compatible demographic or materialist reference. Generic person, team, workplace, praise and request wording do not license assigning a yuppie identity to an otherwise unspecified participant. Professional references use phrases rather than the ambiguous adjective professional by itself; these hints restrict retrieval and are not dating evidence.
